summary: Built and registered the execution for the strongest remaining boundary, a partition between the two configurations. The successor experiment's new split_configurations case collapses a three-voter committed configuration to one voter, snapshots it, makes it three voters again, disconnects the leader from the other two in both directions before stopping it, restarts only the leader with a fresh instance beside it, and then lets both sides elect and commit. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled both sides elected leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums — the restarted side on its one-voter reconstruction, the two peers on the committed three-voter configuration — both sides committed a uniquely named entry and neither side's store held the other's entry; with the flag disabled only the two-peer side led and the restarted side refused with "node is not the leader". Four comparisons are declared: both sides leading and both holding the same term for the flag-enabled case (each predicted violated), cross-side visibility of the two committed entries (also predicted violated), and the flag-disabled control (predicted to hold). Validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so no interpretation was recorded and the split-configuration consequence is not yet part of the account; the harness addition is the turn's substantive work.
